ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ وَقُرْآنٍ مُبِينٍ (١)).
The Exalted's saying (الر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ): this has been mentioned at the beginning of (Surat) al-Raʿd.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (١١)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun in «يَأْتِيهِمْ», and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).
It may also be an adjective (ṣifa) for رَسُولٍ, according to its wording or to its position.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَذَلِكَ نَسْلُكُهُ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ (١٢)).
The Exalted's saying (كَذَلِكَ): i.e. the matter is thus. It may also be an adjective (ṣifa) for an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "an inserting like their mockery".
The hāʾ in (نَسْلُكُهُ) refers back to the mockery, and the hāʾ in (بِهِ) is for the Messenger, or for the Qur'an.
It is also said: (it is) for the mockery as well, and the meaning is: they do not believe because of the mockery; the muḍāf (first term of the construct) was dropped.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they do not believe, while mocking".

ukberi-tibyan:14-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ بَابًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَظَلُّوا فِيهِ يَعْرُجُونَ (١٤) لَقَالُوا إِنَّمَا سُكِّرَتْ أَبْصَارُنَا بَلْ نَحْنُ قَوْمٌ مَسْحُورُونَ (١٥)).
The Exalted's saying (فَظَلُّوا): the pronoun is for the angels; it is also said: for the polytheists. As for the pronoun in «قَالُوا», it is for the polytheists without question.
(سُكِّرَتْ): it is read with tashdīd and ḍamma, and it is transferred (made transitive) by doubling; one says سَكَرَ بَصَرُهُ ("his sight was dazed") and سَكَّرْتُهُ ("I dazed it"). It is also read without tashdīd, and there are two views on it:
The first: it is transitive both lightened and doubled. The second: it is like سُعِدَ; this has been mentioned in (Surat) Hūd.
It is also read with fatḥa on the sīn and kasra on the kāf (سَكِرَتْ), i.e. "were blocked and covered", just as intoxication (al-sukr) covers the mind.
It is also said: it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of أَسْكَرْتُ الشَّيْءَ فَسَكِرَ ("I blocked the thing, so it became blocked"), i.e. it became stopped up.

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَحَفِظْنَاهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ رَجِيمٍ (١٧) إِلَّا مَنِ اسْتَرَقَ السَّمْعَ فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ مُبِينٌ (١٨)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا مَنِ اسْتَرَقَ السَّمْعَ): there are three views on its position:
The first: accusative (naṣb) as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). The second: genitive (jarr) as a badal (substitute), i.e. "except from whoever eavesdrops". The third: nominative (rafʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «فَأَتْبَعَهُ» as the khabar (predicate); the entry of the fāʾ into it is permitted because «مَنْ» means الَّذِي (the one who), or is conditional.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَاهَا وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْزُونٍ (١٩)).
The Exalted's saying (وَالْأَرْضَ): accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We spread out the earth". This is better than the nominative, because it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الْبُرُوج, which the verb has governed.
(وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ): i.e. "and We caused to grow in it various kinds". According to al-Akhfash, «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رُبَمَا يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ كَانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ (٢))
The Exalted's saying (رُبَمَا): it is read with tashdīd (رُبَّمَا) and without it (رُبَمَا), and they are two dialectal forms.
In «رُبَّ» there are eight dialectal forms: among them the two mentioned; the third and fourth are likewise, except that the rāʾ has fatḥa; and the other four are with the tāʾ of the feminine, «رُبَّتَ», so in it there is tashdīd and lightening, and ḍamma and fatḥa on the rāʾ. Concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it is a restraining (kāffa) particle for رُبَّ, so that the verb can come after it, رُبَّ being a preposition (ḥarf jarr). The second: it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), i.e. "many a thing that those who … wish".
And «رُبَّ» is a preposition that is governed only by what comes after it; the governor (ʿāmil) here is omitted, its implied form being: "many a disbeliever who will wish for Islam on the Day of Resurrection have I warned", or something similar. The original use of رُبَّ is for paucity (taqlīl), but here it is for abundance (taktīr) and for affirmation; it has come in this sense frequently in poetry. Most often what comes after it is the past verb, but the future here, because it is certainly true, is treated as the past.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَايِشَ وَمَنْ لَسْتُمْ لَهُ بِرَازِقِينَ (٢٠)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمَنْ لَسْتُمْ): there are two views on its position:
The first: accusative (naṣb) by جَعَلْنَا, and what is meant by مَنْ is the slaves, the slave-women and the beasts, for they are created for our benefit. Al-Zajjāj said: it is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "and We provided livelihood for those for whom you are not …", because the meaning is "We provided livelihood for you and for those for whom you are not …". The second: its position is genitive (jarr), i.e. "for you and for those for whom you are not …"; and this is permitted according to the Kufans.

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِلَّا عِنْدَنَا خَزَائِنُهُ وَمَا نُنَزِّلُهُ إِلَّا بِقَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ (٢١)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا عِنْدَنَا خَزَائِنُهُ): the clause is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) as the khabar (predicate), and «مِنْ شَيْءٍ» is the mubtadaʾ (subject). It may not be an adjective (ṣifa), since there would then be no khabar here.
And (خَزَائِنُهُ) is nominative (marfūʿ) by the adverbial (ẓarf), because it is strengthened by being a khabar; it may also be a mubtadaʾ with the ẓarf as its khabar.
(بِقَدَرٍ): in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَرْسَلْنَا الرِّيَاحَ لَوَاقِحَ فَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَسْقَيْنَاكُمُوهُ وَمَا أَنْتُمْ لَهُ بِخَازِنِينَ (٢٢)).
The Exalted's saying (الرِّيَاحَ): the majority read the plural, which suits what follows it in wording and meaning.
It is also read in the form of the singular (الرِّيحَ), as a generic noun (jins).
Concerning اللَّوَاقِح there are three views:
The first: its original form is مَلَاقِحُ, because one says أَلْقَحَ الرِّيحُ السَّحَابَ ("the wind impregnated the clouds"), just as one says أَلْقَحَ الْفَحْلُ الْأُنْثَى, i.e. "the stallion impregnated the female"; the mīm was dropped because the meaning is clear. Similar to it is الطَّوَائِحُ, whose original is الْمَطَاوِحُ, because it is from أَطَاحَ الشَّيْءَ ("he flung the thing away"). The second view: it is by way of relation (nasab), i.e. "possessing impregnation", as one says طَالِقٌ ("divorced") and طَامِسٌ. The third: it is in its literal sense; one says لَقِحَتِ الرِّيحُ when the wind carries water, and أَلْقَحَتِ الرِّيحُ السَّحَابَ when it makes the clouds carry water, just as you say أَلْقَحَ الْفَحْلُ الْأُنْثَى فَلَقِحَتْ ("the stallion impregnated the female and she conceived"). Its accusative is as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).
(فَأَسْقَيْنَاكُمُوهُ): one says سَقَاهُ and أَسْقَاهُ; they are two dialectal forms. Some distinguish (between them), saying سَقَاهُ لِشَفَتِهِ when he gives him something to drink at once, or pours it into his throat; and أَسْقَاهُ when he provides him with something to drink over a period of time. And one says أَسْقَاهُ when he prays for rain (al-suqyā) for him.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَنَحْنُ الْوَارِثُونَ (٢٣)).
The Exalted's saying (وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ): نَحْنُ here cannot be a separating pronoun (faṣl), for two reasons:
The first: what comes after it is a verb. The second: the lām is with it.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ صَلْصَالٍ مِنْ حَمَأٍ مَسْنُونٍ (٢٦)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنْ حَمَأٍ): in the position of the genitive (jarr) as an adjective (ṣifa) for صَلْصَالٍ.
It may also be a badal (substitute) for صَلْصَالٍ, with the preposition repeated.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْجَانَّ خَلَقْنَاهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ مِنْ نَارِ السَّمُومِ (٢٧)).
The Exalted's saying (وَالْجَانَّ): accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, to match that to which it is conjoined; and if it were read in the nominative, that would be permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِي فَقَعُوا لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ فَسَجَدَ الْمَلَائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ (٣٠)).
[Translator's note: the source quotes verse 29 (فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ … سَاجِدِينَ) together with verse 30 under the single number (٣٠).]
The Exalted's saying (فَقَعُوا لَهُ): the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to قَعُوا, or to «سَاجِدِينَ».
And (أَجْمَعُونَ) is a second tawkīd (emphasis) according to the majority. Some claimed that it conveys what «كُلُّهُمْ» did not convey, namely that it indicates that all of them prostrated at one and the same time. This is far-fetched, because you say جَاءَ الْقَوْمُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ ("the people came, all of them together") even if some of them preceded others; and because, if it were as was claimed, it would be a ḥāl (circumstantial), not a tawkīd.
(إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ): this has been mentioned in (Surat) al-Baqara.
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ اللَّعْنَةَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ (٣٥)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ): it may be governed by اللَّعْنَة, or it may be a ḥāl from it, the governor (ʿāmil) being the (notion of) settledness (al-istiqrār) in «عَلَيْكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَعْلُومٌ (٤)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ): the clause is a naʿt (adjective) for قَرْيَةٍ, as in your saying مَا لَقِيتُ رَجُلًا إِلَّا عَالِمًا ("I met no man except a learned one"). We have mentioned the status of the wāw in the like of this in (Surat) al-Baqara, in His saying: (وَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَوْ مَا تَأْتِينَا بِالْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ (٧)).
The Exalted's saying (لَوْ مَا تَأْتِينَا): it has the sense of لَوْلَا, هَلَّا and أَلَا ("why not"), all of which are for urging (taḥḍīḍ).

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا نُنَزِّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَمَا كَانُوا إِذًا مُنْظَرِينَ (٨)).
The Exalted's saying (مَا نُنَزِّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ): there are many readings of it, all of them clear.
(إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ): in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial), so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted.
It may also be attached to نُنَزِّلُ, and (the bāʾ) then has the sense of seeking aid (istiʿāna).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَافِظُونَ (٩)).
The Exalted's saying (نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا): نَحْنُ here is not a separating pronoun (faṣl), because it does not occur between two nouns; rather it is either a mubtadaʾ (subject) or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of إِنَّ.

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَا أَغْوَيْتَنِي لَأُزَيِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ (٣٩)).
The Exalted's saying (بِمَا أَغْوَيْتَنِي): this has been mentioned in (Surat) al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ (٤٠)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ): an exception from the same kind (istithnāʾ min al-jins). Is the excepted more than half or less? There is disagreement about this, and the correct view is that it is less.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ (٤١)).
The Exalted's saying (عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ): it is said that عَلَى has the sense of إِلَى ("to"), so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to مُسْتَقِيمٍ, or it is a description of صِرَاطٍ. It is also said: it is construed according to the meaning, and the meaning is: "its straightness is incumbent on Me".
It is also read «عَلِيٌّ», i.e. "exalted in rank". What is meant by the path is the religion.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ عِبَادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانٌ إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْغَاوِينَ (٤٢)).
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ): it is said that it is an exception from a different kind (istithnāʾ min ghayr al-jins), because what is meant by عِبَادِي is those who affirm the oneness of Allah, and the follower of Satan is not one who affirms the oneness. It is also said: it is from the same kind, because عِبَادِي is all the morally responsible (al-mukallafūn). It is also said: «إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ» is an exception not from the same kind, because Satan has no sulṭān, i.e. no proof, over any of the servants, and those who follow him — he does not lead them astray by proof but by making things seem attractive.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمَوْعِدُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ).
The Exalted's saying (أَجْمَعِينَ): it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the genitive pronoun.
It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun, and its governor (ʿāmil) is the meaning of the annexation.
As for الْمَوْعِد, if you make it the place itself, it does not govern; but if you assume here the omission of a muḍāf (first term of the construct), it is valid for الْمَوْعِد to govern, the implied wording being: "and Hell is the place of their appointment".

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَهَا سَبْعَةُ أَبْوَابٍ لِكُلِّ بَابٍ مِنْهُمْ جُزْءٌ مَقْسُومٌ (٤٤)).
The Exalted's saying (لَهَا سَبْعَةُ أَبْوَابٍ): it may be a second khabar (predicate), or resumptive (mustaʾnaf). It may not be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جَهَنَّمَ, because «إِنَّ» does not govern the ḥāl.
(مِنْهُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun residing in the adverbial (ẓarf), namely His saying (لِكُلِّ بَابٍ). It may also be a ḥāl from «جُزْءٌ», being a second adjective (ṣifa) of it placed before it.
It may not be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مَقْسُومٌ», because the adjective does not govern the noun it qualifies nor what precedes it; nor can it be an adjective for بَابٍ, because the gate is not of the people.

ukberi-tibyan:45-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ (٤٥) ادْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَامٍ آمِنِينَ (٤٦)).
The Exalted's saying (وَعُيُونٍ ادْخُلُوهَا): it is read in the form of the imperative, and the tanwīn may be given kasra or ḍamma; on this reading the hamza may not be made disjunctive (qaṭʿ).
It is also read with ḍamma on the hamza and kasra on the khāʾ (أُدْخِلُوهَا), as a past verb. On this reading the tanwīn may not be given kasra, because two quiescent letters do not meet; rather it may be given ḍamma by casting the ḍamma of the hamza onto it, and the hamza may also be made disjunctive.
(بِسَلَامٍ): a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "safe", or "greeted with peace".
And (آمِنِينَ) is another ḥāl, a badal (substitute) for the first.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ إِخْوَانًا عَلَى سُرُرٍ مُتَقَابِلِينَ (٤٧)).
The Exalted's saying (إِخْوَانًا): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the adverbial (ẓarf) in His saying (جَنَّاتٍ).
It may also be an anticipated ḥāl (muqaddara) from the agent in «ادْخُلُوهَا», or from the pronoun in «آمِنِينَ».
It is also said: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun made genitive by the annexation (in صُدُورِهِمْ), and its governor (ʿāmil) is the meaning of adherence and inseparability.
(مُتَقَابِلِينَ): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) for إِخْوَان, so that «عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.
It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition (phrase); the preposition is then attached to something omitted, which is an adjective for إِخْوَان.
It (the preposition) may also be attached to إِخْوَان itself, because its meaning is "lined up together"; on this view «مُتَقَابِلِينَ» is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in إِخْوَان.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يَمَسُّهُمْ فِيهَا نَصَبٌ وَمَا هُمْ مِنْهَا بِمُخْرَجِينَ (٤٨)).
The Exalted's saying (لَا يَمَسُّهُمْ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مُتَقَابِلِينَ, or resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
And (مِنْهَا) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to مُخْرَجِينَ.

ukberi-tibyan:49-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (نَبِّئْ عِبَادِي أَنِّي أَنَا الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ (٤٩) وَأَنَّ عَذَابِي هُوَ الْعَذَابُ الْأَلِيمُ (٥٠)).
The Exalted's saying (أَنَا الْغَفُورُ): it may be a tawkīd (emphasis) of the accusative (pronoun), a mubtadaʾ (subject), or a separating pronoun (faṣl). As for His saying «هُوَ الْعَذَابُ», faṣl and mubtadaʾ are permissible in it, but tawkīd is not, because الْعَذَاب is an overt noun, and an overt noun is not emphasised by a pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا سَلَامًا قَالَ إِنَّا مِنْكُمْ وَجِلُونَ (٥٢)).
The Exalted's saying (إِذْ دَخَلُوا): concerning «إِذْ» there are two views. The first: it is an object, i.e. "remember when they entered". The second: it is an adverb of time (ẓarf), and concerning its governor (ʿāmil) there are two views. The first: (the word) ضَيْف itself, for it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). There are two ways of accounting for this. The first: that it governs by itself even though it is used as a description, because its being a description does not strip it of the rules of maṣdars; do you not see that it is not made plural, dual or feminine, just as if it were not used as a description?
This is strengthened by the fact that the description whose place the maṣdar takes may govern. The second way: that there is the omission of a muḍāf in the speech, its implied form being "inform them about the people of Ibrāhīm's ḍayf", i.e. the people of his hospitality; on this view the maṣdar is annexed to its object. The second of the two views on the ẓarf: that the governor is omitted, its implied form being "about the news of the guests".
(فَقَالُوا سَلَامًا): this has been mentioned in (Surat) Hūd.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ أَبَشَّرْتُمُونِي عَلَى أَنْ مَسَّنِيَ الْكِبَرُ فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ (٥٤)).
His saying (عَلَى أَنْ مَسَّنِيَ): it is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "you gave me glad tidings while I am old".
(فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَي): it is read with fatḥa on the nūn, and that is the (proper) way; the nūn is the sign of the nominative (rafʿ).
It is also read with kasra on it, with the yāʾ of the first person omitted; concerning the nūn there are two views:
The first: it is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the nūn of the nominative is dropped because of the heaviness of two identical letters. The first (nūn) was more deserving of being dropped, since if it remained it would have to take kasra, and the nūn of declension is not given kasra lest it become a follower; that has occurred in poetry. The second: the nūn of protection is dropped and the remaining one is the nūn of the nominative, because the verb is nominative, so its sign was retained.
The reading with tashdīd is more sound. [Translator's note: the reading with a doubled nūn (تُبَشِّرُونِّ) is referred to here although it has not been mentioned explicitly above.]

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ وَمَنْ يَقْنَطُ مِنْ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّهِ إِلَّا الضَّالُّونَ (٥٦)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمَنْ يَقْنَطُ): «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يَقْنَطُ» is its khabar (predicate). The wording is interrogative but its meaning is negation; that is why إِلَّا comes after it.
In «يَقْنَطُ» there are two dialectal forms: kasra on the nūn (يَقْنِطُ), its past having fatḥa on it (قَنَطَ); and fatḥa on it (يَقْنَطُ), its past having kasra on it (قَنِطَ). It has been read both ways. The kasra is better, because of His saying (مِنَ الْقَانِطِينَ); both قَانِطٌ and قَنِطٌ are permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:58-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنَا إِلَى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ (٥٨) إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ إِنَّا لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ قَدَّرْنَا إِنَّهَا لَمِنَ الْغَابِرِينَ (٥٩))
[Translator's note: in the standard numbering, إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ قَدَّرْنَا إِنَّهَا لَمِنَ الْغَابِرِينَ is verse 60.]
The Exalted's saying (إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ): it is an exception from a different kind (istithnāʾ min ghayr al-jins), because they were not criminals.
(إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ): there are two views on it:
The first: it is excepted from آلِ لُوطٍ. When an exception comes after an exception, the second excepted (amount) is added to the initial one, as in your saying لَهُ عِنْدِي عَشَرَةٌ إِلَّا أَرْبَعَةً إِلَّا دِرْهَمًا ("he has with me ten, except four, except one dirham"): the dirham is excepted from the four, so it is added to the ten, as if you had said "eleven less four", or "ten less three". The second view: that it is excepted from the object pronoun in «مُنَجُّوهُمْ».
(قَدَّرْنَا): it is read with and without tashdīd, and they are two dialectal forms.
(إِنَّهَا): إِنَّ was given kasra here because of the lām in its khabar (predicate); were it not for the lām, it would have fatḥa.

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَضَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ الْأَمْرَ أَنَّ دَابِرَ هَؤُلَاءِ مَقْطُوعٌ مُصْبِحِينَ (٦٦)).
The Exalted's saying (ذَلِكَ الْأَمْرَ): concerning الْأَمْر there are two views. The first: it is a badal (substitute). The second: it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).
(أَنَّ دَابِرَ): it is a badal for ذَلِكَ, or for الْأَمْر if you make it explicative (bayān). It is also said that its implied form is بِأَنَّ, and the preposition was dropped.
(مَقْطُوعٌ): the khabar (predicate) of «أَنَّ دَابِرَ».
And (مُصْبِحِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from هَؤُلَاءِ. It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مَقْطُوعٌ»; its interpretation is that دَابِر here has the sense of "the last ones of these", so He made it singular and made مَقْطُوع singular because it is its khabar, and مُصْبِحِينَ came according to the meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا أَوَلَمْ نَنْهَكَ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ (٧٠)).
The Exalted's saying (عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ): i.e. from giving hospitality to people (al-ʿālamīn).

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ هَؤُلَاءِ بَنَاتِي إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ (٧١)).
The Exalted's saying (هَؤُلَاءِ بَنَاتِي): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with «بَنَاتِي» as its khabar (predicate); and there is an omission in the speech, i.e. "so marry them".
بَنَاتِي may also be a badal (substitute) or an explicative (bayān), with the khabar omitted, i.e. "are purer for you", as it came in the other verse.
هَؤُلَاءِ may also be in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by an omitted verb, i.e. "he said: marry these".

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ (٧٢)).
The Exalted's saying (إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ): the majority read إِنَّ with kasra because of the lām. It has been read with fatḥa, on the assumption that the lām is redundant (zāʾida); similar to it is the reading of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him: (إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُوا الطَّعَامَ) with fatḥa.
And (يَعْمَهُونَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition (phrase), or from the genitive pronoun in «سَكْرَتِهِمْ», the governor (ʿāmil) being السَّكْرَة or the meaning of the annexation.

ukberi-tibyan:90-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى الْمُقْتَسِمِينَ (٩٠) الَّذِينَ جَعَلُوا الْقُرْآنَ عِضِينَ (٩١)).
The Exalted's saying (كَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا): the kāf is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a naʿt (adjective) for an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "We have given you seven of the oft-repeated (verses), a giving like that which We sent down", or "a sending down like that which We sent down", because آتَيْنَاكَ means "We sent down to you". It is also said that the implied wording is "We gave them enjoyment, an enjoyment like that which We sent down", and the meaning is: We favoured some of them just as We punished some of them.
It is also said that the implied wording is "a sending down like what We sent down", so it is a description of a maṣdar.
It is also said that it is a description of an object, its implied form being: "I warn you of a punishment like the punishment sent down upon الْمُقْتَسِمِينَ". What is meant by الْمُقْتَسِمِين is the people of Ṣāliḥ, who swore together to attack him and his family by night.
It is also said: they are those who divided the Qur'an into poetry, and into sorcery and soothsaying.
It is also said that its implied form is "We will surely ask them all, like what We sent down".
The singular of «عِضِينَ» is عِضَةٌ; its final radical (lām) is dropped, the original being عِضْوَةٌ.
It is also said: what was dropped is a hāʾ, and it is from عَضَهَ يَعْضَهُ, from الْعَضِيهَة, which is slander or calamity.

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاصْدَعْ بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ (٩٤)).
The Exalted's saying (بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ): مَا is maṣdariyya, so there is then nothing omitted.
It may also mean الَّذِي (that which), with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ بِهِ; the original being "with what you are commanded to proclaim openly", then it was dropped because it is known.

ukberi-tibyan:96-96.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَجْعَلُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ (٩٦)).
The Exalted's saying (الَّذِينَ يَجْعَلُونَ): an adjective (ṣifa) for الْمُسْتَهْزِئِين, or accusative by an implied verb, or nominative on the assumption of «هُمْ» ("they are").
